I read the scope last night, but some parts are not clear to me. Who operates the plant today?
The plant is operated by the city water utility. We only design the upgrade.
And what exactly is included in the scope?
The capacity is increased to six hundred liters per second, and two pumping stations are built.
Where are the technical details? I could not find them.
All the equipment is described in Annex B. Every requirement there is mandatory.
Mandatory? Even the brand of the pumps?
No, only the specification. The brand is chosen by the contractor.
Good. And how is the flow rate controlled?
It is measured every hour, and the design is approved by the utility before anything is built.
Last question. Is maintenance included? The board is going to ask me that.
The capacity is increased to six hundred liters per second.
Maintenance is not included in this contract.

Welcome to the North River treatment plant. Before we start the tour, a few rules. Helmets and boots are required in every area after this door. The sewage arrives here from the whole east side of the city, and first it is screened to remove the solids. Then the water is sent to these large tanks, where it is treated by bacteria for about eight hours. Samples are taken every two hours and tested in the lab next door. Photos are allowed, but please do not touch any valve. The tour takes about forty minutes.

Hi Thiago, it is Paul from the utility, with a quick note on how the design review works on our side. Every design is checked by two engineers, and the comments are sent back to you within ten days. Small changes are accepted by email, but a new drawing is required for any change in capacity. Nothing is approved on Fridays, so please do not send anything important that day. Call me if anything is unclear. Thanks.

First, the scope is written and sent to the consultancy. Then, the design is prepared by the consultancy. After that, the design is approved by the utility. Next, the pumping stations are built and the capacity is increased. Finally, the flow rate is measured every hour and the results are sent to the client.
